name: Ch.1 · The Child in the River

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hebrew slaves filled Egypt. Pharaoh ordered every newborn boy thrown into the Nile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One woman hid her son for three months. Then she could hide him no longer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She made a basket of bulrushes, sealed it with pitch, and laid him among the reeds by the riverbank.

lines.speaker: miriam
lines.text: Stay here, little brother. I'll watch from where they cannot see me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe in the Nile. Her maids walked along the bank.

lines.speaker: pharaohs_daughter
lines.text: One of the maids spotted the basket among the flags. She sent her slave to fetch it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She opened it. A child was crying. She felt sorry for him — though she knew what he was.

choices.label: Hide him in the palace 🏛️
choices.note: She keeps the child close. The risk is shared now.

choices.label: Send him back to the river 🌾
choices.note: The Hebrew sister — already watching — steps forward.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His sister asked: "Shall I go and find one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?"

lines.speaker: pharaohs_daughter
lines.text: Yes. Go.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So his own mother took him back, nursed him, and when he was older, returned him to Pharaoh's daughter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She named him Moses — "drawn from water" — and he grew up in the house of the man who ordered Hebrew babies killed.

name: Ch.2 · Exile and the Burning Bush

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Years passed. Moses saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew. He looked around — no one watching.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He struck the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The next day he tried to break up a fight between two Hebrews. One of them turned on him.

lines.speaker: israelite_elder
lines.text: Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you going to kill me like you killed the Egyptian?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pharaoh heard of it. He tried to kill Moses. So Moses ran — into the desert, toward Midian.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He sat by a well. Seven daughters of the priest of Midian came to draw water for their father's flock.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some shepherds drove them away. Moses stood up and helped them. Water for the flock. Shade for the girls.

lines.speaker: zipporah
lines.text: Why have you come? You are an Egyptian.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: I was. I am not now. I am a stranger in a strange land — like you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses settled with Jethro. He married Zipporah. He kept sheep in the wilderness for forty years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One day, near Horeb — the mountain of God — a bush was on fire. And it did not burn up.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Moses. Moses.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: Here I am.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Do not come any closer. Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: I have heard the cry of my people in Egypt. I have seen their suffering. I am come down to deliver them.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: I will be with you. And this will be the sign to you that it is I who sent you: when you have brought the people out, you will worship God on this mountain.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Say to Pharaoh: "Thus says the LORD: Let my people go, so that they may worship me."

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: What if they do not believe me? What if they say the LORD has not appeared to you?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: God gave Moses three signs. A staff that became a serpent. A hand turned leprous and whole again. Water from the Nile turned to blood.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Aaron your brother will speak for you. You will be as God to him; he will be your prophet.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: O Lord, please send someone else.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: What is that in your hand?

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: A staff.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Throw it on the ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Plague after plague had fallen. Water to blood. Frogs. Gnats. Flies. Death of livestock. Boils. Hail. Locusts. Darkness.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Still Pharaoh refused. So one more plague was coming — and there would be no warning.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: On the tenth day of this month, each man is to take a lamb for his family, one lamb per house.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where you eat the lamb.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: When I see the blood, I will pass over you. No destructive plague will touch you when I strike the land of Egypt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Eat it in haste. Sandals on. Staff in hand. This is the LORD's Passover.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At midnight in Egypt — wailing everywhere. Every firstborn son had died, from the prisoner in the dungeon to the firstborn of Pharaoh.

lines.speaker: pharaoh
lines.text: Get up! Get out from among my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have asked. Take your flocks too. Go!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night — the Israelites had been slaves in Egypt for four hundred and thirty years — they finally left.

name: Ch.5 · A Path Through the Water

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pharaoh changed his mind. Six hundred of his best chariots pursued the Israelites to the edge of the sea.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Trapped. Water before them. Army behind them. No way forward.

lines.speaker: israelite_elder
lines.text: Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us out here to die?!

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the LORD will bring you today.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea to divide it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: All that night a strong east wind drove the sea back. The water divided. The seabed was dry ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses stretched out his hand. The people walked through on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Egyptians followed — every horse and chariot, every driver — into the middle of the sea.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At daybreak, the LORD looked down from the pillar of fire and cloud and threw the Egyptian army into confusion.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The waters rushed back and covered the chariots and horsemen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Not one of them survived. Israel saw the great power the LORD displayed against the Egyptians, and the people feared the LORD.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three days into the wilderness — no water. The people came to a place called Marah. The water there was bitter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They grumbled against Moses. "What are we to drink?"

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: Lord, what shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The LORD showed Moses a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A month later — the whole company had run out of food. Again the grumbling began.

lines.speaker: israelite_elder
lines.text: If only we had died by the LORD's hand in Egypt, where we sat around pots of meat and ate all the food we wanted!

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: I will rain down bread from heaven for you. The people are to go out each day and gather enough for that day.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: On the sixth day they are to prepare what they bring in, and it is to be twice as much as they gather on the other days.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That evening quail came and covered the camp. In the morning there was thin flakes like frost on the ground.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: This is the bread the Lord has given you to eat. Gather an omer from each person.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some gathered much. Some gathered little. Each measured exactly an omer — no more, no less.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Those who gathered much had nothing left over. Those who gathered little had no shortage. Each had gathered just as much as they needed.

choices.label: Trust that tomorrow's bread will come 🌅
choices.note: No one hoards. No one goes hungry. A new kind of daily dependence.

choices.label: Keep a little extra — just in case 📦
choices.note: Moses warned them. By morning the extra was wormy and rotten.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the third month after the Israelites left Egypt, they came to the desert of Sinai. They camped at the foot of the mountain.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: If you will obey me fully and keep my covenant, then out of all nations you will be my treasured possession.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: All the people answered together: "We will do everything the LORD has said."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, with a thick cloud over the mountain, and a very loud trumpet blast.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The whole mountain trembled violently. Smoke went up like a furnace. The LORD descended on it in fire.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. You shall have no other gods before me.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Do not misuse the name of the LORD your God. Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Honour your father and your mother.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Do not covet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: All that the LORD says, we will do. All that the LORD says, we will obey.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder. Then Moses spoke and the voice of God answered him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights. Down below, the people grew restless.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They went to Aaron. "Make us gods who will go before us. As for this fellow Moses — we don't know what has happened to him."

lines.speaker: aaron
lines.text: Give me your gold — your earrings, your rings, your chains." He collected it. He shaped it with a tool. He made a golden calf.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tomorrow we will feast to the LORD! They offered sacrifices and sat down to eat and drink. Then they got up to indulge in revelry.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Go down, because your people, whom you brought up out of Egypt, have become corrupt. They have been quick to turn away from what I commanded them.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: O LORD, why have you brought trouble on this people? Turn from your fierce anger. Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, your servants.

choices.label: Plead for the people — every one of them 🙏
choices.note: Moses offers himself to be blotted out instead. God does not take the offer — but He relents the destruction.

choices.label: Speak for yourself — walk away from this 🚶
choices.note: Moses has reached the end of what he can carry alone. He turns back to the camp anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses came down from the mountain. In his hands were the two tablets of the covenant, inscribed on both sides.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When he approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned. He threw the tablets out of his hands, breaking them at the foot of the mountain.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: Who is on the LORD's side? Come to me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sons of Levi gathered to him. He said: "Each man strap a sword to his side. Go back and forth through the camp from one end to the other. Each man kill his brother and friend and neighbour."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: About three thousand people died that day. Then Moses returned to the LORD. "Please forgive your people. Blot me out of the book you have written if you will not."

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Whoever has sinned against me I will blot out of my book. Now go, lead the people to the place I spoke of. My angel will go before you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the LORD said to Moses: "Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Spies went up into Canaan — twelve of them, one from each tribe. After forty days they came back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The land flows with milk and honey — but the people who live there are powerful, and the cities are fortified and very large!

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: We should go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly do it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But the other spies spoke against Caleb. The whole assembly talked about stoning them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night all the people of the community raised their voices and wept aloud.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Not one of you will enter the land I swore with uplifted hand to make your home. Your children will be wanderers in the wilderness for forty years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Years passed. Provision kept coming. Manna every morning. Quail some evenings. Water from the rock. Their clothes did not wear out. Their feet did not swell.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But one day, at Meribah, there was no water again. The people quarrelled with Moses. Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Because you did not trust in me enough to honour me as holy in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this community into the land I give them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses — who had brought them out of Egypt — would not bring them in. Joshua would.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Forty years after the basket on the Nile, the people stood at the edge of the Jordan — and one man would not cross with them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses was now a hundred and twenty years old. His eyes were not weak. His legs were not feeble.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Go up this mountain in the Abarim Range — Mount Nebo — and look at the land I am giving the Israelites as their own possession.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Moses commissioned Joshua son of Nun. "Be strong and courageous, for you must go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their ancestors to give them."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses wrote down the law. He gave it to the priests and to all the elders of Israel. He commanded them: read this law aloud every seven years, at the festival of shelters.

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: I am now a hundred and twenty years old and I am no longer able to lead you. The LORD has said to me, "You will not cross the Jordan."

lines.speaker: moses
lines.text: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid. The LORD your God goes with you. He will never leave you nor forsake you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There the LORD showed him the whole land — Gilead as far as Dan, all of Naphtali, the territory of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Mediterranean Sea.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Negev, the whole region of the Jordan — the land from Jericho, the city of palms, all the way to Zoar.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in Moab, as the LORD had said. He buried him in the valley, in Moab — and no one knows where his grave is to this day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died. Yet his eyes were not weak. His legs were not feeble.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Israelites grieved for Moses for thirty days. Then Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom. The people obeyed him — and the story of Moses was over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But the story he carried was not over.
